items.title: Oscar Peterson interviewed by Joe Williams, Majesty of the Seas, May 31, 1995
items.q: I went the other way. I went the way of trios, because I was also a Nat Cole fan, as you know.

ctx.x: Yeah, he was one of a kind, really.

That’s right. Well Art was a consummate soloist. He was the epitome of a solo pianist, regardless of what medium we are talking about — jazz, classical, or what have you. And that’s what he set out to do and he did that. I went the other way. I went the way of trios, because I was also a Nat Cole fan, as you know.

Well you like to stomp too. I mean you like the swing and the smoke comes out, the instrument breathes, the piano breathes, and everything happens, you know. The things that I’ve seen you do in Chicago, in Montreal and in Toronto, you know, the things that I’ve seen you do, and in Hollywood — oh my God, the afternoon sessions. Basin Street. Stuff like that.
